original_test_intent: Verify the BMC I2C-9 management path through the named HMC-7 element reaches the intended M.2 sideband endpoint and returns a valid device-specific register response.
original_method: Map BMC I2C-9 to Linux bus8; clarify HMC-7 identity/function and its route to a specific M.2 slot; identify0x6a/register0x00d5 protocol; capture owner and device-health baseline; avoid broad scan; run one bounded combined read; decode six bytes and correlate them with M.2 serial/slot/sideband identity and controller error status without changing storage or physical seating.
manual_activity: BMC/HMC/storage owner supplies the HMC-7 and M.2 sideband topology, slot/device identity, register decoder and safe ownership/recovery. No physical M.2 handling is inferred.
required_inputs: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-9 to Linux bus8 through the exact HMC-7 element to an M.2 slot
Definition of HMC-7 naming and whether it is controller/channel/mux/bridge
Identity of address0x6a and proof it belongs to the intended installed M.2 endpoint
Vendor definition for register0x00d5, write-pointer safety and six returned bytes
M.2 slot/BDF/serial/model/firmware correlation and sideband-versus-PCIe identity
Bus owner/driver, timeout/NACK/error criteria and BMC/HMC/M.2 recovery
safety_requirements: Do not run broad quick-write discovery; query only the approved0x6a endpoint
Confirm the two-byte pointer is non-mutating for the exact sideband device
Coordinate with BMC/HMC driver ownership and avoid concurrent raw access
Do not remove/reseat M.2, alter PCIe/storage state or write sideband registers
Perform one bounded read; abort on identity mismatch, invalid length/value, NACK, timeout, stuck bus or storage/management health regression
agent_execution_scope: Collect BMC/HMC/M.2 route, slot/serial identity, owner and read-only health/error baseline
After approval, execute one exact sideband read and decode/correlate all six bytes
Do not probe/solder/reseat, scan blindly, access storage data, write registers, reset controllers, auto-retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Clarify HMC-7 and approve BMC I2C-9/bus8/M.2 route
Approve0x6a/register0x00d5 protocol and expected six-byte decoder
Approve ownership, timeouts, abort and recovery
Review sideband response/slot identity/health evidence and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incorrect physical-only substitution; source provides a remote combined read and does not request M.2 handling.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Omit broad `i2cdetect -q`. After route/protocol approval, retain `i2ctransfer -y 8 w2@0x6a 0x00 0xd5 r6` as one bounded read; decode six bytes and bind them to the approved M.2 slot/serial and HMC route.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC bus8, address0x6a, register bytes0x00/0xd5, r6, BMC I2C-9, HMC-7, M.2, PID1114953 and 15/5-minute scope are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform a single read-only sideband query and correlate decoded content to the exact installed M.2 device and controller path.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds route/slot identity, six-byte acceptance and ownership controls while rejecting unsourced probing/reseat and unsafe generic scanning.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A six-byte reply from0x6a proves only that some sideband responder exists; it does not prove the named HMC-7 path or intended M.2 unless content and slot identity are correlated.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Unknown sideband semantics can affect management state, and a healthy sideband reply does not validate PCIe data-path performance or media integrity.

project_override_considerations: Wistron I2C policy requires BMC controller/bus, target address, management path, vendor protocol and expected reply. Storage device identity must be immutable and must not be inferred from index alone.
expected_evidence: PID topology for BMC I2C-9/bus8/HMC-7/M.2 sideband path
BMC/HMC identities and exact M.2 slot/BDF/serial/model/firmware mapping
Owner/driver state and pre-read storage/management health
Vendor register0x00d5 definition and expected six-byte matrix
Timestamped exact transfer with stdout/stderr, exit code, latency, raw and decoded bytes
Pre/post BMC/HMC/sideband/storage error logs, unchanged device availability and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source does not define HMC-7, map logical I2C-9 to bus8, identify0x6a/register0x00d5 or provide expected six bytes/M.2 slot identity. Prior reviews additionally invent physical probing and M.2 handling.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The management-sideband purpose and candidate read are clear; authoritative topology, decoder and owner approval are supplyable inputs, so it is RPUC.

Confirm no physical probing/reseat is required unless separately scoped.

review_improvement: Restores the remote M.2 sideband test, removes invented physical handling and makes HMC route, immutable device identity and six-byte response semantics auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: Nothing in the Procedure asks to touch the M.2 module; the test is framed as a BMC management-bus reply. The real coverage gap is attribution: the unexplained HMC-7 path and0x6a response must be bound to a specific installed device, since PCIe enumeration and sideband addressing are separate identities. A decoded bounded read can prove functional sideband reachability without risking reseat or data-path disturbance.
